meta.title: earmilk siblings: drivers and electronics for the bookshelf and desk/pint cartons
method: WebFetch/curl were blocked, so every figure is a search-engine extract of the cited maker datasheet or retailer page. Open the datasheet before cutting metal or wood.

Marking: a field listed under confidence.confirmed agreed in two or more independent places; confidence.unconfirmed means one place only, a value I derived or inferred, or a value read from an unlabelled drawing; confidence.conflicts lists disagreements and which value was used.

Box numbers are my own Thiele-Small calculation (closed box; Small vented box with QL = 7). Vented results are the lowest f3 with peak <= +0.5 dB and response >= -1 dB above 1.6 x f3. 'dsp_boost' is the asymptotic Linkwitz-transform boost (40*log10(fc/target)). Ports: one flanged end, 17 m/s at full Xmax for the minimum diameter.
The shared web-search budget ran out before Dayton RS180/RS180P-8A could be checked; those are not in this file.
Prices are snapshots (several pages were months old); USD unless stated. Currency conversions are mine.

conventions.sensitivity: dB SPL at 2.83 V / 1 m unless stated
conventions.depth_behind_baffle_mm: from the back of the flange to the rear of the motor (mounting depth)
conventions.effective_cone_d_mm: 2*sqrt(Sd/pi): the visible cone plus about half the surround, use for CAD

geometry.assumptions: Square plan W; body height 2.2 W; roof rise 0.385 W (37.6 deg pitch, matching the flagship); solid gable block on top (not counted as air volume); 18 mm birch walls for the bookshelf with separate bottom and top panels; net = gross x 0.95 (bracing, wadding) - driver - port - 3.5 L for a sealed Hypex FusionAmp sub-compartment where stated (the sibling amps research, research/amps.md, estimates 3.5-4 L).

roof_waveguide.mouth_width: about 0.5 W (100 mm at W 200, 110 at 220, 125 at 250; 50 mm on the pint)
roof_waveguide.usable_length_along_slope: slope 0.63 W minus margins: about 110 / 121 / 132 / 138 mm for W 200 / 220 / 240 / 250
roof_waveguide.oblique_axis_warning: If the tweeter axis is horizontal (or tilted only slightly) instead of normal to the slope, the mouth on the slope is an oblique section: the effective mouth height perpendicular to the axis is only about 0.61 x the along-slope length, i.e. about 67 / 74 / 81 / 84 mm for W 200 / 220 / 240 / 250 and about 34 mm on the pint. The waveguide is then elliptical (about 110 x 74 mm at W 220).
roof_waveguide.vertical_extent_rule: With a near-horizontal axis the faceplate's full diameter stands vertically inside the roof block: the roof is only 0.385 W tall (85 mm at W 220, 38 mm on the pint), so 100-104 mm faceplates cannot sit wholly in the bookshelf roof and must poke down into the body.
roof_waveguide.centre_to_centre: W 220 with a 171 mm woofer frame 12 mm below the eave and the tweeter 30% up the slope: about 127 mm, against a wavelength of 156 mm at 2.2 kHz (150 mm frame: about 117 mm). Keep the woofer as high as possible.

recommended.woofer: SB Acoustics SB17NRX2C35-8 (171 mm frame, cutout 144.9, 4 x 4.3 on 159 PCD, 75 mm behind baffle)
recommended.tweeter: Scan-Speak Illuminator D3004/602200 (62 mm faceplate, Fs 440 Hz) at the throat of the carved waveguide; R3004/602200 is the ring-radiator twin with a confirmed US price
recommended.amp: Hypex FusionAmp FA122 (plate 315 x 120 mm, recess 291 x 96 mm) in a sealed sub-compartment on the rear panel (about 3.5-4 L displaced)
recommended.crossover: LR4 at 2.0-2.2 kHz in the FA122 DSP; tweeter level and waveguide EQ from measurement
recommended.box: W 220, body 484, 18 mm birch: 15.2 L gross, about 10.1 L net after a 3.5 L sealed FA122 compartment. Sealed: fc 70 Hz, Qtc 0.80, f3 62.5 Hz; +7.6 dB low shelf (Linkwitz transform) gives f3 45 Hz. Excursion limit at 45 Hz about 85 dB at 1 m per speaker (full space). Fill loosely with wadding.
recommended.alt_box: W 240: about 15.2 L net, vented fb 34 Hz, port 35 x 137 mm (or 41 x 193 mm), f3 47 Hz without boost. W 250: 18.1 L, fb 36 Hz, port 41 x 142 mm, f3 43 Hz.
why: The 171 mm frame is 0.78 W, the same visual ratio as the flagship's 314 mm woofer on 390 mm.
The D3004/602200 has the smallest faceplate (62 mm) and the lowest Fs (440 Hz) of the realistic options, so a 2-2.2 kHz LR4 is safe even with a small, shallow waveguide.
The FA122 gives DSP crossover, baffle-step and low-shelf EQ and 125 W/4 ohm (75 W/8 ohm) per channel in a plate narrow enough for a 220 mm rear panel.

budget.name: Bookshelf, budget: W 220 mm, active vented 2-way, all Parts Express
budget.woofer: Dayton RS150P-8A (150 mm frame, cutout 122, 74 mm deep). Upgrade at the same frame size: SB15NRX2C30-8 (cutout 123.9, 78.9 deep) for about 8-10 Hz more bass
budget.tweeter: Dayton ND25FN-4 element (41 mm, no faceplate) at the throat of a fully carved waveguide
budget.amp: Dayton KABD-250 (2 x 50 W, ADAU1701) on a KABD-PMV4 panel (120 x 95 mm) + 24 V 4 A supply + one KPX programmer
budget.box: About 13.6 L net (board amp takes almost no volume). RS150P-8A vented fb 50 Hz, port 35 x 57 mm, f3 51 Hz. With SB15NRX2C30-8: fb 39 Hz, port 35 x 109 mm, f3 43 Hz.
budget.cost_each_usd: about 190 (woofer 55, tweeter 15, amp 64, panel n/f, supply about 20; KPX 38 shared)
why: One 150 mm frame model in CAD covers both the RS150P-8A and the SB15NRX2C30-8.
An element tweeter lets the carved roof form the whole waveguide from a 41 mm throat, which suits the small mouth best.
The KABD-250 board is about 1/7 the cost of the FA122 and still gives a programmable crossover; the trade is SigmaStudio and lower power.

recommended.name: Pint, recommended: active 2-way
recommended.woofer: Dayton ND65-4 (64 mm round, cutout 52, 48 deep) - or SB65WBAC25-4 if you want a 64 mm square frame
recommended.tweeter: SB Acoustics SB14ST-C000-4 (24.2 mm face, screwed from behind with M4) in the roof scoop
recommended.amp: Dayton KABD-430 (or Wondom JAB4): one board per stereo pair; crate of six = three boards, 12 channels
recommended.crossover: LR4 at 3.5-4 kHz; high-pass the woofer at 70-80 Hz
recommended.box: Sealed, about 1.3 L net (9 mm walls give 1.36 L gross, 6 mm give 1.61 L): fc 106 Hz, Qtc 0.72, f3 104 Hz; +4.9 dB shelf gives f3 80 Hz.
why: The ND65-4 has the lowest Fs and most excursion of the 2.5 in drivers that fit a 100 mm face.
The SB14ST is the only real dome small enough (24 mm) for the 50 x 34 mm effective scoop, and its rear M4 mount suits a solid wooden roof.

budget.name: Pint, budget: passive, one amp channel per pint
budget.tweeter: Dayton ND16FA-6 (32.5 mm press-fit) through one series capacitor (about 4.7 uF), or no tweeter
budget.amp: Crate of six: two JAB4 / KABD-430 boards (8 channels, 6 used). A single pair: one KABD-230 or JAB3+
budget.box: Same sealed 1.3 L; use the board DSP for EQ and the 70-80 Hz high-pass
why: Halves the channel count and needs no crossover DSP; about USD 33 of drivers per pint.

fits_in_crate: Wondom JAB4 / Dayton KABD-430 (91 x 69 x 20 mm each; three for six active pints)
Wondom JAB5 / Dayton KABD-4100 (more power than needed)
